mostWorthwhile.text: Burying peat as carbon was the strongest moment: the explanation connected waterlogged conditions to the long-term storage of material made by photosynthesis.

leastWorthwhile.text: The final nutrient-return sequence felt somewhat drawn out: returned nutrients were an extra intermediate before the predictable renewing forest.

surprise.text: Fallen wood and water produced fungi directly; the decomposition route made sense, but that creation was a compressed leap.

arbitrary.text: Forest plus air producing fallen wood lacked a clear mechanism, even though the result served the chapter’s goals.

continue.text: Yes. The contrast between buried carbon and nutrients cycling back into growth made me curious about what other connections the world could reveal, despite some predictable intermediate steps.
